facts.fact: ANIP says that since 1 April 2021 every birth declaration is made to the RNPP, which issues the child's NPI and automatically enters the birth in the national civil status file, both files being run by the one agency ANIP.

ANIP says births declared to the RNPP register automatically in the civil status file, and a declared death activates the 'deceased' status in the identification system and is registered automatically with civil status.

Triomphe Mag, citing ANIP's report of 24 February 2026, says births declared and registered at the single desk in ten pilot health facilities since 20 August 2025 give the child a personal identification number (NPI) by SMS within 48 hours and update the RNPP.
Triomphe Mag, citing ANIP's report on the pilot (20 August 2025 to 20 February 2026), says the pilot produced 30,160 number updates, 12,182 captured signatures and 798 recorded portraits in the RNPP.
